items.title: Explosion at the Yorktown Navy Mine Depot: 1943
items.channel_title: The History Guy: History Deserves to Be Remembered
items.description:
In 1943 the Yorktown, Virginia, Naval Mine Depot manufactured explosive ordnance and loaded it onto ships in the York River bound for the battlefields of WWII.  On November 16th, a massive explosion rocked the Depot, leaving enormous craters and shattering glass for miles around. 

Check out our new shop for fun The History Guy merchandise:
https://thehistoryguy-shop.fourthwall.com/products/thg-history

This is original content based on research by The History Guy. Images in the Public Domain ar
items.why_watch: The History Guy digs up a genuinely obscure WWII home-front disaster — a 1943 munitions explosion at a Virginia naval depot that shattered windows for miles yet barely made history books. It's a tight 17 minutes on the industrial dangers behind the war effort, the kind of story that reminds you how much happened stateside that never got commemorated. If you like history that feels newly discovered rather than retold, this is that.

This video is my take on 3B1B's Summer of Math Exposition (SoME) competition. It explains in pretty intuitive terms how ideas from topology (or "rubber geometry") can be used in neuroscience, to he
items.why_watch: Neuroscience PhD student Artem Kirsanov explains how the brain encodes behavior not as scattered neural firing, but as low-dimensional geometric shapes — 'manifolds' — embedded in high-dimensional activity space. The visual approach, inspired by 3Blue1Brown's style, makes an genuinely abstract concept feel intuitive without dumbing it down. If you've ever wondered how a brain that fires billions of neurons still produces structured, predictable behavior, this video offers a real answer.

items.title: The Sunset Cabin | Guided Sleep Story (The Haven) | Deep Sleep
items.description:
A calming, high-quality sleep talk‑down set in a cozy sunset cabin the peace of The Haven. Designed to help you unwind, relax, and fall into deep sleep with soothing nature imagery, soothing music and a real human‑spoken narration. 
Travel through the Haven to a cosy hilltop cabin overlooking the sea, where a glowing sunset, warm lamplight and complete safety gently carry you into deep sleep.

This guided sleep meditation story can help you reach a state of deep relaxation and fall asleep fast.
items.why_watch: The Honest Guys have been making sleep narrations for over a decade, and this cabin-at-sunset entry showcases exactly why they have a loyal following — unhurried pacing, specific sensory detail (warm lamplight, sea view, the Haven's quiet), and a voice that treats rest as the actual goal rather than a side effect of content. It's a functional sleep tool, not ambient filler, and at under 20 minutes it won't outlast your ability to stay awake.
